newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraq-Turkey pipeline oil quality no problem - Botas.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-Turkey pipeline oil quality no problem - Botas.

text.p: An official from Turkey's state-run pipeline company Botas said on Monday there was no quality problem with the oil trapped inside the Iraq-Turkey pipeline to be used for oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.

"There is no quality problem in the pipeline," Teoman Alta, deputy head of the procurement and operations department at Botas, told Reuters when asked about the approximately 12 million barrels of oil inside the pipeline.
The 986-km (616-mile) twin pipeline from Iraq's Kirkuk oilfields to Turkey's southern Ceyhan port has remained idle since the U.N. trade embargo on Iraq after it invaded Iraq in 1990.
Market sources and some officials earlier said the oil inside could have deteriorated in time and be used to produce lower-tier products like asphalt and kerosene.
Alta said Botas was ready for export operations after a test on metering equipment by the Netherlands-based firm Saybolt, which said the pipeline was functioning properly.
"We are ready for operation, but we are waiting for the final decision from the United Nations," Alta said.
U.N. officials said at the weekend U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali is ready to give the go-ahead for the oil-for-food plan on Monday, barring last minute obstacles.
The deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months for the purchase of badly needed food, medicine and other necessities for its people.
Alta said he did not know who would take the initial oil exports, which could go into tankers or into a refinery owned by the Turkish state refiner Tupras.
The 12 storage tanks at Ceyhan were not yet full and could be used for a couple of days before the loading of tankers, Alta said. He added that tankers have not yet been assigned.
Botas expects to earn around $50 million in transportation fees from the $2 billion Iraqi oil sales, he said.
